**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part:** Wheat/cereal leaf
- **Pattern:** Distinct longitudinal (parallel to leaf veins) yellow-orange stripes running the length of the leaf
- **Color:** Bright orange-yellow pustules/lesions arranged in linear stripes along veins, with intervening green tissue still partially visible
- **Texture:** The orange areas appear as small pustule-like masses arranged in rows/stripes
- **Distribution:** Stripes are consistent and parallel, not random blotches

**Reasoning:**

The hallmark feature here is the **yellow-orange pustules arranged in distinct longitudinal stripes** parallel to the leaf veins. This is the classic presentation of **Stripe Rust** (also called Yellow Rust, caused by *Puccinia striiformis*). Key distinguishing features:
- Pustules are small and arranged in neat linear rows/stripes (vs. Wheat Leaf Rust which has scattered, random circular pustules)
- Yellow-orange color (vs. Stem Rust which produces brick-red/brown larger pustules)
- Affects leaf blade in parallel stripe pattern following vascular tissue

This is definitively **Stripe Rust**, not Wheat Leaf Rust (which has randomly distributed orange-red uredinia) or Stem Rust (darker, larger pustules on stems).
